topics.label: Introduction to complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture and frames complement within the broader study of immunology.

topics.label: Fundamentals, nomenclature, and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational overview, naming conventions, and core C3 activation mechanism of the complement system.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation and trigger threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the three activation pathways—alternative, lectin, and classical—and the accumulation required to reach the trigger threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the primary effector functions triggered by complement activation: opsonization, inflammation, and pathogen lysis via the membrane attack complex.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the protective regulatory proteins and mechanisms that prevent complement from damaging host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical presentations of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the clinical manifestations and disease risks resulting from deficiencies in specific complement components and regulators.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion mechanisms and applications of staphylococcal protein A
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how pathogens evade complement attack and how staphylococcal protein A is applied in research and medicine.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture on complement and previews the upcoming session on adaptive immunity.
